title: fix(plugin-security): a predicate write composes the platform ownership floor per row, as the by-id write does
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvVRcFWKrfWeG5jzPb

Part of #35802 (the `controlled_by_parent` half of the card's repro is left for a decision, see Acceptance notes)


Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 业务用户用条件批量修改或删除（流程、脚本、服务端批量更新）时，拥有「修改全部」的经理、不是创建人的记录负责人、以及被授予「编辑」共享的人（仅修改），现在能改到他们逐条修改也能改的那些记录；以前只改到自己创建的记录，结果照样报成功。
- 属于记录级权限，替在 18.6.0 上搭审批对象的外部开发者解决「批量改悄悄少改」的问题，延续之前逐条修改那次修复。
- 能改的行只多不少，每一行都按逐条修改时的同一判定放行；但一次批量修改仍是全成或全败：新纳入的某一行若不满足检查规则，整次修改会被拒，以前这种情况会只改创建人的那几行并报成功。普通成员批量修改大量别人的记录会变慢（一万行约五秒）。出问题可以直接撤回本 PR，不涉及数据迁移。
- 要你定一件事：新纳入的行不满足检查规则时，是整次拒绝（现状，需要按收紧申报）还是跳过该行只改其余的。

## What changes

`packages/plugins/plugin-security` only. The #5492 floor composition (the sharing service's `allow` replaces the platform's own `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes`; `abstain` and `deny` keep it) now runs per matched row on the PREDICATE write path, which never reached it because it sits under `extractSingleId(opCtx) != null` in step 2.7.

- **Step 3, RLS injection** (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`). For an addressed predicate update or delete (`addressedPredicateWrite`) by a non-delegated caller, after the existing read question (`readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`, the readable ids the caller's predicate matches, capped at 10,000 with a refusal above), when the platform floor is in play for the caller (`predicateWriteFloorRelief`):
  1. `replaced`: `computeLayeredRlsFilter` with `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor`, the Layer 1 the by-id write of a row composes once its floor is replaced. Where it is not null, an authored `using` policy remains, and the relief answers null with no read and no verdict. Policies compose by OR only, so a row `floored` refuses fails every authored policy too, and its by-id write is refused as well: replacing the floor can add no row there (L2 S2);
  2. one read, under the caller's context, of which matched ids the floored Layer 1 already admits; nothing is asked about them;
  3. for every other matched id, the by-id gate's own floor decision, `resolvePreImageFloorDrop` (`predicateWriteFloorDropIds`, new in `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`, asked in batches of 25);
  4. Layer 1 becomes `floored OR id IN dropIds`. Layer 0 is recomposed exactly as it stood.
- **Step 3.6, the per-row `check`.** A predicate update's row whose floor step 3 replaced is held to the check `computeWriteCheckFilter` composes with `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` (what step 2.7 passes for a by-id `allow`); every other row keeps `checkParts`. Without this the floor's `using`, defaulted as the check, refused on the new row the write it had just admitted (ablation leg 2 below).
- Untouched: Layer 0, every app-authored policy (where one remains, no row is added), the verb boundary (`delete` asks `checkDelete`, and the sharing middleware's bulk delete scope stays owner-only), ADR-0066 ① (Modify All does not skip business RLS on an ordinary object), the delegated path (both floors kept, as on the by-id path), nested predicate writes (no readable-id list, floor kept), and `masterGateCoversThisWrite` (never set on the predicate path).

## Why

#35802, measured on 18.6.0 by an outside builder: a predicate update by a Modify All manager or a non-creator owner changed only the rows the caller created and answered success. Measured on this branch with the fix ablated (= `origin/main` f44758b21e), rows changed by a predicate write over the 4-row owner x creator matrix vs the by-id path:

| caller | verb | predicate, before | by id | predicate, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) ALICE, owns r1 r2, created r1 r3 | update | r1 | r1 r2 | r1 r2 |
| (a) ALICE | delete | r1 | r1 r2 | r1 r2 |
| (b) BOB, owns r3 r4, created none | update | none | r3 r4 | r3 r4 |
| (b) BOB | delete | none | r3 r4 | r3 r4 |
| (c) CAROL, created r2 r4, owns none | update | none | none | none |
| (c) CAROL | delete | none | none | none |
| (d) Modify All manager | update | none | r1 r2 r3 r4 | r1 r2 r3 r4 |
| (d) Modify All manager | delete | none | r1 r2 r3 r4 | r1 r2 r3 r4 |
| edit-share target, shares on r2 r3 | update | none | r2 r3 | r2 r3 |
| edit-share target | delete | none | none | none |

## Tests

New `src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts`, 27 cases, on the `isolated` tenancy posture so Layer 0 is composed on every write: the real `SecurityPlugin` over a real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), the real `SharingService` and its middleware, and the shipped `member_default` floor (the rig of `controlled-by-parent-owner-may-edit.test.ts`). Each case runs the predicate write on one copy of the matrix and a by-id write of each id on a second copy, asserts the two sets are equal row for row, and names the expected set. Cases: the four callers and the edit-share target, each x predicate update and predicate delete (the edit-share delete stays floored: ADR-0111 D3); a Modify All holder under an authored update policy (`stage == 'open'`), which still binds the rows whose floor is replaced; the CONTROL, an owner-less object where sharing abstains, both verbs, where a member still changes only the rows they created; and a row outside the predicate is never touched. Round 2 adds: the verdicts each predicate write asked, recorded on the real sharing service (the floor-admitted rows are never asked about; a delete asks `checkDelete` and never `checkEdit`; no verdict under an authored `using` policy); five on-behalf-of cases (BOB for CAROL, a member with Modify All, both verbs; ALICE for CAROL; ALICE for ERIN, an admin with Modify All, both verbs), each equal to the by-id set; the owner-creator under an authored widener writing the closed row she created, as before; the S1 case below; 60 candidates across three verdict batches; the composed predicate still naming the organization (Layer 0); `idsOfReadableScope` keeping bigint ids; and three direct pins on `predicateWriteFloorDropIds` (the verb it is handed, delegation, at most 25 in flight). The objects are ordinary tenant business objects on purpose: on a tenancy-disabled object a Modify All holder skips business RLS entirely and the floor would never be composed (measured: the first draft of the file used `tenancy.enabled: false` and its manager cases passed for that reason).

A new file rather than a `describe` in `row-write-widener-composition.test.ts` (the #5492 file): that file's engine double cannot run a predicate write's composed AST, the nested read questions, or the sharing middleware's bulk scope, and each of them decides a row here.

## Acceptance notes

- **The admit set is a union; the outcome is not (L2 S1, the seat rules the arm).** Layer 1 is `floored OR id IN dropIds`: every row it adds is one the by-id path admits for the same caller, and no row today's predicate write matches is removed. But a predicate update applies to all of its matched rows or to none. Measured: ALICE under a check-only policy (`region == 'emea'`), r1 hers and EMEA, r2 hers, created by CAROL, in APAC. Before this PR the predicate update answered success with r1 written. On this head it is refused whole, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, nothing written. By id, r1 is written and r2 is refused 403. The same follows from a validation rule, a hook or a `readonlyWhen` lock on a newly matched row. The changeset now says so. The case is pinned as the current answer.
- **Measured corner where the two paths still differ, as before this PR:** an owner-creator holding an authored update widener (`stage == 'open'`) on a CLOSED row they created and own. By id: 403, because dropping the floor from an OR of permissive policies leaves the widener alone. By predicate: written, as before. Pinned. Reported as a by-id finding, not copied.
- **Not fixed here: the card's own repro object.** On a `controlled_by_parent` detail, record sharing abstains and the by-id write drops the floor through `masterGateCoversThisWrite` (the master gate), which `RlsFilterOptions` documents the bulk path must not set ("a separate decision"). Measured on this branch with the same rig: the master's owner, predicate update over 4 detail rows changes r1 r3 (created by them), by id all 4; a Modify All manager, predicate 0, by id 4. Hence `Part of`.
- **Cost, measured** (SQLite in memory, shared box, one run each; origin/main, then this head). A member updating 1,000 readable rows owned by others: 44 ms with 3 driver reads, then 1,085 ms with 1,000 `checkEdit` and 2,004 reads, writing 0 rows either way. The same at 10,000: 47 ms, then 5,298 ms with 10,000 verdicts and 20,004 reads. A Modify All holder at 10,000: 47 ms writing 0 rows, then 1,796 ms with 10,000 verdicts and 10,003 reads, writing all 10,000. A Modify All holder under an authored `using` policy, 10,000 closed rows: 1,629 ms with 10,000 verdicts at the round-1 head, then 45 ms with none on this head (S2). Bounded by the existing 10,000 readable-row cap, which refuses above it before anything runs. The changeset names the member cost.
- Nested predicate writes (a hook's or cascade's own write under the caller's context) are not addressed predicate writes, carry no readable-id list, and keep the floor as before.
- Response shape unchanged: no "rows dropped by the floor" report was added.
- Not taken from L2: N3 (a `!preImageFloorOpts` guard on the relief). Measured on the compare-and-set shape, BOB updating `where: { id: r4, stage: 'open' }, multi: true`: origin/main writes nothing (1 verdict), this head writes r4 (2 verdicts), and this head with the guard writes nothing again (1 verdict). Step 3 does not read step 2.7's decision, so the guard would bring the reported under-write back on that shape. The cost is one extra verdict for one row. N6 (`image.id`) is also not taken: a predicate update never carries a truthy payload `id` (`resolveEngineUpdateDispatch` routes it by id, or refuses), and a falsy one is never in `dropIds`.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `predicateWriteFloorRelief` (end of file): the union and the floor-admitted read.
2. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, step 3.6 hunk (`floorDropJudge`): which rows get the floor-replaced check.
3. `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`, `predicateWriteFloorDropIds`: the per-row by-id decision.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` shows 27 passed. Flip `if (rlsFilter && layered.layer1 && !delegatorSets)` to `if (false && ...)` and the matrix cases go red.

All readings below are at head `267ccece2d` (the last commit is changeset-only; the ablations ran on `7b89b3ceb4`, the same code).

<details>
<summary>plugin-security suite, typecheck, build: all green</summary>

- `pnpm typecheck` then `pnpm build` in the package: lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. `check:test-typecheck: OK ... 0 file(s) / 0 error(s)`; `check-dts-emitted: @objectstack/plugin-security - 2/2 declared declaration file(s) present.`
- Full suite: `Test Files  285 passed (285)`, `Tests  7095 passed | 45 skipped (7140)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- New file alone: `Tests  27 passed (27)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Round 2 ablations: 7 legs red, 1 equivalent mutant, every restore clean</summary>

Each leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode: the anchor hit once and then zero times, the blob moved, the file ran, and the restore proved blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty.

- Verb (`'update'` in place of `rlsOperation` in the relief), blob `869cbad82cdf -> 3f018c0744b9`. The round-1 pins (14, run beside it) stay GREEN, as the L2 predicted: the sharing middleware's bulk delete scope is the owner set, so no row moves. The new verdict pins go RED, 2 of 27: ALICE's and DAVE's predicate deletes asked `edit:` verdicts.
- `!delegatorSets` at the relief, blob `-> 9eab6beaab22`: RED, 5 of 27. The delegated updates were refused whole, and the delegated deletes wrote extra rows (BOB for CAROL wrote `r4`; ALICE for ERIN wrote `r1 r2 r3`).
- `!delegatorSets` at the step 3.6 check, blob `-> ad03a10d8fe7`: GREEN, 27 of 27. This is an equivalent mutant. On a delegated write the relief never runs, so no row is in `predicateFloorDropIds`, and the floor-dropped judge is computed and never read.
- Floor-admitted set-aside, blob `-> d7f80d96aaab`: RED, 2 of 27. ALICE's update asked `edit:r1..r4`, not `edit:r2 r4`, and her delete did the same.
- Batch loop ran once, blob `5569e873e4a4 -> 628fcd57a9e3`: RED, 2 of 27. Only 25 of the 60 rows were asked about, and the direct helper pin failed too.
- Batch slice one short, blob `-> 819033e6e42f`: RED, 2 of 27.
- Layer 0 recompose dropped, blob `-> 5d9ad8cb55d5`: RED, 1 of 27. The composed predicate no longer names the organization.
- S2 early return removed, blob `-> e54f5695cc91`: RED, 1 of 27. Without it the added arm has no authored policy, so NARROW's closed `r1 r4` were matched and the write was refused whole (`PERMISSION_DENIED`). The early return is what keeps an authored `using` policy binding on this shape.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Derived gates: 71 derived, 69 exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED</summary>

`dispatch-gates --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `267ccece2d` derived the same 71 families as round 1 (4 paths, +955 / -9). Each ran once, and its exit code was recorded before any pipe. Reconciliation: `71 derived famil(ies) accounted for, 69 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`. The two NOT MEASURED families are `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n`, both exit 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET: they read the whole workspace's `dist/` and the built CLI. CI runs both. `check-governed-merges --pr 35914`: NOT governed, 964 changed lines.

</details>
